stderr:

The investigation reveals that while the application Pods are healthy, the Kubernetes Service `app` is failing to route traffic because it has no associated endpoints.

Upon inspection of the Service configuration, I found a critical mismatch in the `selector`:
```yaml
  selector:
    app: does-not-match
```
This selector is instructing the Service to only route traffic to Pods that have the label `app` with the value `does-not-match`. Since the application Pods are running and healthy (implied by their names and status, typically they would be labeled with a value like `app`), the Service is not finding any matching Pods, resulting in the `<none>` status on the endpoints.

I will correct the Service selector to match the application Pods, assuming the standard label `app: app` is used on the healthy Pods.

### Change Applied
I am updating the `app` Service definition to change the selector from `app: does-not-match` to `app: app`.
